chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sitting of a man after the dawn prayer until the emergence of the sun is more effective in seeking sustenance than sailing the sea.'

So I said, 'What if a man has a need that he fears missing out on?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can set out for it, and let him remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for he is in the follow-up (prayer) as long as he remains upon ablution.'
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of sitting after Fajr prayer and how does ablution relate to sustenance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual and material benefits of sitting in devotion after the Fajr prayer until sunrise, stating it is more effective for gaining sustenance than maritime trade. When asked about urgent needs that require leaving, he advises that one may depart while maintaining ritual purity, as the state of wudu keeps one in a continuous state of prayerful remembrance. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that wudu is not merely a ritual prerequisite but a sustained spiritual state that preserves divine connection and facilitates divine provision (rizq) even during daily activities.
